chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked, 'How much should be given to the man from the zakat?' He said.
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'When you give, make him self-sufficient.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of zakat to give according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the concept of zakat from mere almsgiving to a mechanism for economic liberation, instructing recipients to be made 'self-sufficient' (غني) rather than merely sustained. This qualitative standard reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *istighna* (independence) as the ultimate goal of charity, distinguishing it from the fixed minimums (*nisab*) applicable to the distribution itself. It underscores the ethical imperative that zakat should empower the poor to exit the cycle of dependency, aligning with the broader jurisprudential principle of maximizing benefit (*maslaha*) for the recipient.
